title: Controlling Temporal Pseudo-Label Marginals for Stable Online Test-Time Adaptation
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A plug-in module added to a standard teacher-student pipeline balances recent pseudo-label marginals toward a target prior to stabilize adaptation.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, green highlighted module inside white baseline
description: A left-to-right block diagram of a teacher-student pipeline. At left, two photos of a motorcyclist show the input view x_u and an augmented view x_v. These feed a Teacher f_φ box on top and a Student f_θ box on the bottom. A dashed arrow labeled 'EMA update' runs from the student to the teacher. The teacher's softmax output goes through a stop-gradient (sg) into a Consistency loss box at top right. A large green rounded region labeled 'SCALAR · temporal marginal regulation' sits in the middle. It holds four green blocks in a chain: FIFO logit window, Sinkhorn balancing (with a Target prior π arrow from above), Current-batch targets, and SCALAR loss. The student output feeds both losses. A bottom-right box gives the combined loss L = (1−λ)L_cons + λL_bal. A legend at bottom left explains the white and green colors and sg. The green region draws the eye first.
caption: Overview of the SCALAR framework. White blocks denote the baseline teacher–student CTTA pipeline; green blocks denote the added SCALAR module. Given an input view xu for the teacher branch and an augmented view xv for the student branch, the teacher produces logits zu and probabilities qu = softmax(zu). Recent teacher logits are stored in a FIFO window and converted to probabilities P, which are balanced toward a target prior π via Sinkhorn to produce balanced targets ˜qu. The student produces logits sv and probabilities pv, and is optimized using a mixture of the baseline consistency loss and the SCALAR loss based on ˜qu. Gradients are stopped through teacher-derived targets, marked by sg, and teacher parameters are updated via EMA. Here Lcons ≡Lconsistency and Lbal = CE(sg[˜qu], pv).
abstract: Continual Test-Time Adaptation (CTTA) methods update models online using a stream of unlabeled data to overcome distribution shifts encountered at test time. However, CTTA is often unstable, as it can reinforce biases in early predictions and increasingly predict only a few classes, resulting in drift or even collapse. In this paper, we identify narrowing pseudo-label class usage as an indicator of CTTA instability and quantify this behavior. Most existing methods have attempted to address this issue by either selecting reliable adaptation samples or re-weighting the loss to encourage diverse pseudo-labels, but they do not explicitly enforce a class marginal over a temporal window. Instead, we propose Sinkhorn Class-Marginal Regularization (SCALAR), a simple plug-and-play module that controls the pseudo-label distribution over a short temporal window. SCALAR works by maintaining recent predictions in a buffer, balancing their class distribution via the Sinkhorn algorithm to match a specified target distribution, and using the balanced soft targets for adaptation. Without changing the model architecture, SCALAR maintains the per-step runtime and increases the peak allocated GPU memory by only 10 MB on ImageNet-C. Our method is particularly effective on skewed, non-stationary data with severe distribution shifts, where SCALAR significantly alleviates drift and collapse when combined with existing stabilization methods based on entropy or diversity.
